gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-hedvig-letters-s: Stencilia leaves generous gaps where its curves end, which gives the headings a cut-out, structural look. Hedvig Letters Sans follows with small letters nearly as tall as its capitals, so paragraphs feel friendly and compact.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-heebo: Striking in the heading and plain-spoken below, this pairing puts Stencilia's gapped curves above a text with a tall central band. Heebo's body can be sized up a notch for comfort.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-hind-guntur: Hind Guntur draws tall lowercase forms with no thick-thin shift, like stamped metal type in a steel cable outline. And Stencilia does the striking, structural job up top, while the sans-serif below simply keeps text moving.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-hind-madurai: Stencilia's spacious gaps at its curve ends make the heading look cut and assembled, almost like a stencil. And Hind Madurai answers with lowercase that fills the line like capitals, so the heading and text feel built from the same ribbon.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-hind-mysuru: Sharp, built, and a bit stenciled. Hind Mysuru backs it up with lowercase tops pressing near the ascender height and no calligraphic thinning, so Stencilia's structural headings get a body that is dependable and uniform.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-hind-siliguri: Structural from the first glance, Stencilia cuts open gaps into its curves and sets a bold stage above the text. Hind Siliguri settles into a flat gray hum of constant line weight, and the sans-serif body feels approachable beside it.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-hind-vadodara: Stencilia's headings have spacious gaps where curves finish, giving every title a cut-out look. Hind Vadodara then keeps big, open-looking e and a shapes with tall bowls, so a long stretch of sans text stays clean and easy to follow.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-huninn: Huninn reads modern and businesslike, with lowercase bodies that rise close to cap height and s terminals that stay clear of the stem. Stencilia handles the striking part; Huninn handles the steady reading.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-karla: Karla reads modern and friendly, with a gaping c opening and a middle band so tall the line looks stocky. Stencilia is best at striking structure; Karla is best at easy text.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-kedebideri: Stencilia opens its curve terminals wide and keeps a compact gap between x-height and ascender line, which makes headings look structural and striking. Kedebideri's skyward x-height is the sans-serif body's strongest card.
